blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — In the forests of the southern Philippines lives another endangered eagle that has received far less scientific and public attention than the critically endangered Philippine eagle. The South Philippine hawk-eagle (Nisaetus pinskeri), found only in the Philippines, is considered the country’s second most threatened eagle, with an estimated 600 to 800 mature individuals remaining in the wild and its population continuing to decline. Now, Filipino scientists have unlocked part of the bird’s genetic history, providing a scientific foundation for future research and conservation efforts to prevent its extinction.
